## Highlights

- Website scans skip rendering a page only when its plain HTML carried all of the text the browser
  showed at the page's last render. In v0.5.75, nine tenths of the text was enough, so a change
  drawn only by the page's JavaScript could go unnoticed. Pages whose plain HTML falls short are
  rendered on every scan. This was a known issue in v0.5.75.
  [Crawling](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/knowledge/crawling)
  · [#4451](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4451)
- A comment you are editing in a task discussion keeps its editor and draft when new comments push
  the discussion past 100 rows, whether or not the editor has focus. An open delete confirmation
  or actor preview stays open the same way. This was a known issue in v0.5.75.
  [#4460](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4460)
- Keyboard focus can now move into a task's agent preview and reach **View more**. Escape closes
  the preview and returns focus to where it opened. This was a known issue in v0.5.75.
  [#4457](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4457)
- If the code for the embedding alert, the **New project** dialog or the document preview fails to
  load, for example while offline, the dashboard stays in place. The alert is left out, the
  **New project** dialog closes, and the document preview says "The document preview could not be
  loaded. Try again." with a **Try again** button, instead of replacing the chat transcript. This
  was a known issue in v0.5.75.
  [#4458](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4458)
- When a task holds more than 64 deliverables, a deliverable replaced under the same name now
  counts as the newest, so the next run stages it. Deliverables written before this release keep
  their earlier order until they are written again. This was a known issue in v0.5.75.
  [#4452](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4452)
- Resumed task runs receive the current task description, including an explicit notice when it
  has been cleared. Their prompt reflects edits made since the earlier run instead of relying
  only on the description retained in the conversation.
  [#4479](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4479)
- A project agent explicitly granted `task_delegate_review` can hand a pending native agent review
  to another independent agent in the same project. The handoff checks the captured approval,
  source run and evidence revision, preserves the task's status, implementation assignment and
  future reviewer settings, and starts no run. The recipient needs `task_review` and its own
  eligible review run to decide the review.
  [Task automation](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/task-automation)
  · [#4482](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4482)
- Usage charts add up the selected days, weeks or months in the database, so a large
  organization's 90-day view no longer reaches the 20,000-row read limit early and shows partial
  totals. The current and previous periods stay separate even when they share a week or month.
  This was a known issue in v0.5.75.
  [#4474](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4474)
- Governance's **Model access** and **Default models** editors show their scope, role and mode
  options, such as Team, Admin or Allowlist, in the session's language; German and French
  sessions saw them in English before. **Budgets** also translates role options and table targets.
  Stored rules are unchanged.
  [#4462](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4462)
  · [#4478](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4478)
- When an immediate **Model access** save fails, the editor restores the previous controls,
  including after confirming a change that affects default models. Fresh saved configuration
  updates the open editor and closes edit or delete dialogs whose selected rule may have changed.
  A later failed save preserves an earlier successful save while the cached policy is unchanged.
  [#4266](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4266)
- The agent details panel uses the names shown elsewhere in the interface: **Connectors** and
  **Plattform-Tools** in German, and **Skills** and **Connectors** in French, where "Compétences"
  is the name of a different Governance feature.
  [#4461](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4461)
- Runtime selectors and related guides consistently use **Agent runtime** in English,
  **Agent-Laufzeit** in German and **Environnement d'agent** in French. Saved runtime values,
  API fields and documentation URLs are unchanged.
  [#4480](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4480)
- The website's German and French pages use the app's names for Knowledge and Automations
  (Wissen and Automatisierungen, Connaissances and Automatisations) and correct several German
  product terms.
  [#4472](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4472)
- Screen readers no longer announce the language, website, Shopify and Enter-key icons on their
  own; an icon is announced only when it is given a name. The contacts table's language column has
  a header that screen readers announce as "Language", and the composer's send hint is read as
  "Enter to send".
  [#4468](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4468)
- Math rendering uses KaTeX 0.18.2, which fixes GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7 (CVE-2026-103923, low
  severity): earlier versions could treat properties inherited from an already polluted
  `Object.prototype`, such as `trust`, as renderer options. KaTeX 0.18 prefixes its internal CSS
  class names; Tale's own styles don't use them.
  [#4422](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4422)
- A project's **Environment** tab says that its credentials are stored for the project and aren't
  passed to agent runs yet, and points to the agent's **Secrets** grants instead. Its editor applies
  the server's rule for names (an uppercase letter first, then uppercase letters, digits or
  underscores, at most 64 characters) and explains an invalid name in the session's language. The
  projects overview documents the tab in English, German and French, including who can manage the
  credentials and how to replace or remove a value.
  [Project credentials](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/overview#environment-credentials)
  · [#4469](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4469)
  · [#4463](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4463)
- The CLI reference documents `tale deploy --bundle <directory> --configuration-only`. It applies
  only managed instructions, agent tool grants and automations to the healthy runtime of an
  already-ready deployment, without a pre-deploy snapshot or restart; use it when only those
  change and runtime and identity inputs stay the same. The new `agent-tools` resource updates
  an existing agent's tool set while preserving its model, instructions and secret grants.
  German and French guides also correct interface labels, including provider, storage and
  approval controls.
  [CLI install](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/install/cli-install)
  · [#4470](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4470)
  · [#4464](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4464)
  · [#4477](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4477)
  · [#4482](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4482)
- The guides describe the **Password change required** screen. Members see it at sign-in after an
  administrator sets or resets their password, or when it expires under the organization's
  rotation policy, and set a new password before continuing; an administrator's reset also signs
  the member out of all sessions.
  [When a password change is required](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/member/preferences#when-a-password-change-is-required)
  · [#4465](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4465)

## Upgrade notes

- Back up the application and knowledge databases, configuration, keys and external stores
  before deploying. On startup, the knowledge database container (`knowledge-db` in Compose)
  applies the knowledge-corpus migration `00000000000014_website_url_strict_change_check.sql` from
  this release's `db` image to `tale_knowledge`. It adds nullable `etag_v2`, `last_modified_v2`
  and `probe_hash_v2` columns to `public_web.website_urls`, clears the change checks that earlier
  releases stored once, and adds a trigger that discards any check written to the earlier columns.
  The previous platform keeps working on the migrated database during a rolling deploy, but its
  scans render every page, because its checks are discarded. Upgrade the knowledge database
  container to this release's `db` image and wait for its migrations to finish before starting the
  new platform images. Keep the columns and the trigger during a rollback: the migration has no
  down step. The first scan of each website after the upgrade renders every HTML page again; later
  scans skip unchanged pages as described above.
  [Upgrade and recover](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/operate/upgrades)
  · [#4451](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4451)
- If upgrading directly from v0.5.74 or earlier, also apply the
  [v0.5.75 upgrade notes](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/blob/v0.5.75/.github/release-notes/v0.5.75.md);
  these steps remain required even if you skip running v0.5.75. Upgrade `knowledge-db` to the
  v0.5.76 release `db` image and wait for knowledge-corpus migrations
  `00000000000013_website_url_change_check.sql` and
  `00000000000014_website_url_strict_change_check.sql` to complete, in that order, before starting
  the new platform images. The backend applies `0153_two_factor_first_required_sign_in.sql` on
  startup; it is forward-only, so retain its column during an image rollback. Update any pinned
  `SANDBOX_RUNTIME_IMAGE` to the matching v0.5.76 runtime image, which includes the sharp security
  update. Use the release's Tale CLI when updating retained 0.5 Compose runtimes so it can adopt
  the `static-assets` named volume; existing data volumes and host mounts must still match the
  managed topology.
- Relative to v0.5.75, this release adds no application database migration, environment variable,
  or Compose service; knowledge-corpus migration 14 remains required as described above.
  To adopt `agent-tools` or captured review delegation, first deploy this release's runtime and
  use its matching Tale CLI. Older runtimes refuse the new capability. Grants are explicit:
  an `agent-tools` resource replaces the complete tool set, so include every grant to retain;
  `[]` clears it. Review the native plan and read back the applied tools. This release does not
  automatically grant review or delegation authority, change secret grants, or route pending
  reviews. Runtime upgrades still use a full deployment; configuration-only applies to later
  changes against that ready compatible runtime.
  [CLI install](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/install/cli-install)
  · [#4482](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4482)
- Known issues in this release:
  - The projects overview still describes the **Environment** editor's earlier name check and the
    tab's earlier wording about task runtimes. Where they differ, the tab and its editor are
    current.
    [#4454](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4454)
